programs.target: L1 (tested on up, down; best on up)
programs.mechanism: weather-compensated supply curve: supply setpoint falls as outdoor temperature rises
programs.refute: fitted slope is zero or positive, or the curve alone explains no more variance than a constant supply

programs.mechanism: weather curve with an upper cap on supply water temperature
programs.refute: the fitted cap lies above every supply value the curve reaches, so it never binds

programs.target: L1 (tested on up, down; best on up)
programs.mechanism: weather curve with a lower floor on supply water temperature
programs.refute: the fitted floor lies below every supply value the curve reaches, so it never binds

programs.target: L1 (tested on up, down; best on down)
programs.expr: base + slope * T_out + where(month() >= dry, boost, OFF)
programs.mechanism: seasonal autumn-drying boost added to the weather curve during and after the drying month
programs.refute: the fitted boost is zero, or the fitted month places the boost outside the heating season

programs.target: L1 (tested on up, down; best on up)
programs.mechanism: weather curve driven by a delayed outdoor temperature, representing building mass or sensor lag
programs.refute: the fitted delay is zero, or delaying T_out does not reduce held-out error versus the undelayed curve

programs.target: L2 (tested on up, down; best on up)
programs.from_text: Two heating circuits, L1 and L2, one outdoor sensor
programs.mechanism: second heating circuit shares the outdoor sensor but has its own parallel weather curve with a fixed offset
programs.refute: the fitted offset is zero, or L2 supply is better explained by the same curve as L1

programs.from_text: Radiators. Most radiators have no thermostatic valve. The TV room radiator has an analog thermostatic valve, almost closed.
programs.mechanism: radiator circuit weather curve plus room-temperature feedback; the nearly closed TV valve appears as a small effective gain
programs.refute: the fitted room feedback gain is zero, or the TV room is no better fit with feedback than without

programs.from_text: Floor heating. Kitchen also gets warm air rising from downstairs through the open space and balcony.
programs.expr: max(base + slope * T_out, mn) + gain * (sp - T_room)
programs.mechanism: floor-heating weather curve with a minimum supply floor and room feedback; the rising warm air from downstairs acts as an unmodelled heat input that the room feedback partially compensates
programs.refute: the fitted minimum floor never binds, or the kitchen is no better explained with room feedback than by the curve alone

not_expressible.from_text: Indirect district heating substation; domestic hot water outside this controller
not_expressible.why: This describes plant topology and a heat source outside the controller. The language has no district-heating, substation, or DHW state, so it cannot be written as a control law for any target.

not_expressible.from_text: L1 Menovesi - L1 supply water temperature; L2 Menovesi - L2 supply water temperature; Ulkolämpö - outdoor temperature
not_expressible.why: These are measurement labels, not control mechanisms. They name signals already available in the language and imply no setpoint action.
